It dials out to this instance; nothing on your machine listens. It decides which directories and modes remote work may use, whatever is asked here.

Notifications come through UnifiedPush, with no Google services: the distributor app you chose carries them, encrypted for this phone only.
To be told when a reply is ready, install a UnifiedPush distributor such as ntfy, then come back here. Without one, the app shows new replies when it is open.
Notifications are on for this instance.
No distributor was chosen, so notifications are still off.

Make LLeMbas the phone\'s digital assistant: choose it under Default apps › Digital assistant app. Then holding the power button, the assist gesture or the lock screen\'s shortcut opens it over whatever is on screen.
On Samsung phones: Settings › Advanced features › Side button › Press and hold › Digital assistant.
Read the answer aloud when asked by voice
The update could not be fetched.
Allow LLeMbas to install updates, then check again.
The download did not match the release and was discarded.
%1$s is available. Tap to open its release page.

At most once a day, when the app starts, it asks your instance which release goes with it (an older instance: the list of releases on GitHub) and tells you in a notification when there is a newer one. Nothing about you is sent anywhere else. On by default in a beta, off otherwise.
Offer test versions as well as releases. On by default when this app is itself a beta.
A newer version is available. Tap to open its release page.
Sign in to a LLeMbas instance in the app first.
The screen\'s text and a screenshot go with your next question.
The screen\'s text goes with your next question.
A screenshot goes with your next question.
Summarise what is on my screen.
Translate what is on my screen into English.
Explain what is on my screen.
Hold the power button to open the assistant over any app, or use the Quick Settings tile.
This reply is waiting for your answer: open it in the app.
I listen again after each answer. Say “stop” to end.
stop|that\'s all|that is all|that\'s it|goodbye|bye|enough|end|thank you that\'s all|cancel
After a spoken answer is read aloud, the assistant listens again — until you say “stop”, tap End, or say nothing for a few seconds. Works with a headset.
No wake word unless you want one: Settings › Assistant › Wake word turns on LLeMbas\'s own, on this phone.
Off by default. Say the phrase and the assistant opens, listening, over whatever app is on screen.
Not in this build. The F-Droid build has no wake-word engine, because F-Droid builds every library from source; the build from llembas.eu has one.
What you say, then a short pause: it counts once you stop. In English, whatever language the app is in: the engine only knows English speech.
A Google phone or speaker nearby will answer too.
Starts by mistake least often. You may have to say the phrase more clearly, or twice.
Hears you most easily, also from further away. Starts by mistake more often.
For ten seconds, shows whether your phrase is heard, without opening the assistant.
Not heard in ten seconds. Try closer to the phone, in a quieter moment, or a higher sensitivity.
Turn the wake word on first.
Only while the screen is on
Off: it listens with the screen off too, at more cost to the battery.
Let it run in the background

Some phones (Samsung, Xiaomi, Huawei, OnePlus and others) stop background apps to save battery, and the wake word with them. Exempt LLeMbas from battery optimisation here; dontkillmyapp.com explains your phone\'s own settings.

Nothing leaves the phone before the word. The microphone\'s sound goes only to the wake-word engine on the phone and is not kept, and the notification stays up the whole time it listens. The phrases are English; the engine is sherpa-onnx (open source).

It costs battery: the microphone stays on and the phone\'s processor checks every moment of sound, without the low-power chip the built-in assistant uses. It pauses in battery saver, while the assistant is open and, unless you change it, with the screen off. After a restart, tap its notification to start it again.
The wake word is not listening
Tap to start it again. If Android asks, allow the microphone.
Wake word hears nothing: another app has the microphone, or the phone\'s microphone is switched off
Wake word is not working: this build has no engine
Wake word is not working: its model could not be unpacked on this phone
Wake word is not working: the engine did not start
Wake word is not working: the microphone did not start

Nothing leaves the phone until you say it.
Wake word paused: the screen is off
Wake word paused: battery saver is on

LLeMbas can open by itself over other apps only as the phone\'s digital assistant app.
LLeMbas is not the digital assistant app
So the wake word cannot open the assistant over other apps: you get a notification to tap. To open by voice anywhere, tap here and choose LLeMbas as the digital assistant app.

Choose LLeMbas as the digital assistant app again: tap here, pick another app, then LLeMbas. Until then the long press opens it as an ordinary screen, and the wake word can only send a notification.
LLeMbas is the assistant, but Android has not connected it right now
Until it does, the wake word cannot open the sheet by itself. Tap for the system\'s assistant setting: choosing another app and then LLeMbas again connects it.
Could not open by itself — tap to ask
Listen for the wake word again
The phone restarted. Tap to start listening again.
Summarise my notifications: what needs my attention?
Let the assistant read my notifications when I ask
Ask “summarise my notifications”, or tap the chip in the assistant.

Not in this build. Reading notifications needs the “notifications” build of LLeMbas, because Google Play Protect blocks installing an app from outside the Play Store that can read them. It is the same app with the same signature: on the release page, the file ending in -notifications.apk installs over this one.
This is the “notifications” build: install the update from its release page, the file ending in -notifications.apk.
Given. Android\'s switch for it is in the system\'s settings.
Not given yet. Tap to open Android\'s switch for LLeMbas.

Off by default. When you ask, the text of the notifications on your phone right now (app, title, text) goes with that one question to your instance and its model. Nothing is read before you ask, the app keeps none of it, and none is read while the phone is locked. Android\'s notification access lets an app see every notification, so it is yours to give and to take back.

Lets “add a stop” and searches near you work with a route you set up in OsmAnd itself: LLeMbas asks OsmAnd where you are and where the route goes. Allow LLeMbas in OsmAnd first (its connected apps, with Location); OsmAnd tells you if it is not allowed.

A model may offer to do things on this phone — set an alarm, add an event, draft a message, start a route. Nothing happens until you tap Do it on its card, and never while the phone is locked. Google Maps starts a route with a few stops but cannot add one to a route already running or be told to stop; OsmAnd can.
Unlock the phone first, then tap Do it.
Google Maps cannot add a stop to a running route: it starts the route again, through the stop.
Google Maps cannot be told to stop: end the route there.
The calendar opens with the event filled in; you save it.
Opens a draft; you send it yourself.
The dialler opens with the number; you place the call.
Opens the setting; you change it.
Runs your automation (Tasker unless another app is named).
The phone\'s speech recogniser stopped. Try again, or choose LLeMbas under Settings › Voice input.
Start listening when the assistant opens
Your instance\'s speech-to-text, through the server. The recording goes to your instance and nowhere else.
The phone\'s own recogniser. The words appear as you speak; the recording goes wherever that recogniser sends it.
This phone has no speech recogniser of its own.

Used by the assistant and by the microphone in a chat. With LLeMbas the assistant shows the words a moment behind you and a pause sends them, and a chat writes them down when you stop; with the phone\'s recogniser they appear as you speak.
What should LLeMbas do with it? (optional)
Ask by voice or text, or carry on the last assistant chat. Shows nothing from your account.
